cells.tense: You are standing in the first clear look at something and it has not been cut into a plan yet.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you're growing and write down what you actually see about it today. Read it back tomorrow and change what's wrong.
cells.core:
You're seeing something new clearly and you haven't rushed to name what it should become. That's harder than it sounds. A lot of people, the moment they get a clear look, start building. You're letting it be what it is first.

It shows in how you tend. You notice what's actually growing instead of what you meant to grow, and you give that the conditions it needs without demanding it hurry. This kind of clarity is the rarest part. Plenty of people watch carefully and immediately ask it to bloom. Don't let what you see get pinned to the calendar. Write down what you see today, and keep the page readable so tomorrow has somewhere to land.
cells.sheetLine: You see it clearly and you're not rushing to name it.
cells.verb: seeing clearly before there's anything yet to see
cells.place: in the care of what's still growing

cells.tense: You are trying to see what this becomes before you've let it become anything.
cells.ask: Today, look at what you're growing for five minutes and ask what's true right now. Then do whatever that requires — nothing more.
cells.core:
You're watching for a future version. When you tend this thing, you're checking it against what it's supposed to turn into — how fast, how good, whether it's on track. The checking has become a test.

Here's the cost. You can't see what's in front of you when you're standing where it needs to be in a year. The care is still there; the direction is all forward. Notice the impulse to check again, and this time stay with what's actually in front of you. Whatever you see now is the only thing there is to work with. Interest in where it's going isn't the same as seeing where it is. Let one day be enough for one day.
cells.sheetLine: You're checking the future instead of seeing the present.
cells.verb: seeing clearly before there's anything yet to see
cells.place: in the care of what's still growing

cells.tense: You are still looking at something you stopped being able to see.
cells.ask: Name one thing you're growing out loud — to the wall if no one's there. Then pick the one next step and do it.
cells.core:
The care is still happening. You show up, you handle what needs handling. But you stopped being able to look at this thing and actually take in what it is now. You're working from a picture from before, and the picture has been running the job.

Nothing here needs more feeling. Feeling into it again won't bring your eyes back. What brings them back is doing the next concrete thing and letting the looking happen as part of the doing. Pick one step you can finish today, do it, and you'll find your eyes came along. Take one clear look at something small.
cells.sheetLine: You're tending it from a picture, not from sight.
cells.verb: seeing clearly before there's anything yet to see
cells.place: in the care of what's still growing

lint.detail: "the looking" — a verb turned into a mystical noun

cells.tense: You are already seeing what's happening here clearly and calling it something else.
cells.ask: Tell one person something you've noticed about what you're growing — no fixing, no plan. Just what you saw.
cells.core:
Somewhere along the way you started seeing this thing as it actually is. You notice the small changes, the way it's leaning, what it actually needs versus what it's supposed to need. That's already doing the work — it's the reason your care has been as good as it has.

But you don't call it that. You'd say you're just being careful, or just handling it. It gets filed as logistics. So here's what's true: you are the one who looked and saw it, and that's worth saying out loud once. It's yours, not the situation's. Somebody would notice if you stopped. Notice it yourself first.
cells.sheetLine: You're already seeing it clearly. You're calling it being careful.
cells.verb: seeing clearly before there's anything yet to see
cells.place: in the care of what's still growing

attempts.check: The record says the first clear seeing has arrived and hasn't cut anything yet, but it does not say the person is looking at a child, a project, or any particular thing they tend — the cells must keep the growing thing unnamed. A reader could fairly say 'Actually I can't see anything clearly right now,' so each ask is framed as offering the seeing that's already there, not manufacturing it, and the Too Little ask works on a capacity, not on a feeling. The sentence that serves me more than them would be anything about light and radiance shining from within — that's the medicine's vocabulary, not the kitchen's, and I've kept it out.
